Hospital Admission History and Physical
Date: 09/16/2026
Patient: Casey Schiller, 78-year-old male

Chief Complaint:
Admitted 09/16/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 9/10 despite IV analgesia.

History of Present Illness:
Mr. Schiller presents with severe back pain that has necessitated hospital admission. The pain is described as intense and unrelenting.

Past Medical History:
Includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both well controlled.

Physical Examination:
Vital signs are stable. On examination, tenderness is noted over the lumbar spine. Neurological examination reveals no focal deficits.

Assessment:
Severe back pain requiring inpatient management.

Plan:
Continue monitoring pain levels and vital signs closely. Initiate appropriate diagnostic workup to determine underlying cause. Consult relevant specialties as needed for further evaluation and management.

notes.text:
Radiology Report
Date: 09/09/2026
Patient: Casey Schiller, 78-year-old male

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/09/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute compression fracture at the T11 vertebral body characterized by bone marrow edema visible on STIR sequences, consistent with an osteoporotic fracture.

No other acute abnormalities are noted in the thoracic or lumbar spine on this MRI study.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/20/2026
Patient: Casey Schiller, 78-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 08/31/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 3 weeks before this visit. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Assessment:
The patient presents with a vertebral compression fracture corresponding to the site of localized pain.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Further management will be guided by bone density results and clinical follow-up.
